idiom_name: SQLAlchemy JSON / PickleType column (TypeDecorator for a typed codec)
implementation_notes: SQLAlchemy ships both ends of the pattern: JSON stores dict/list payloads in the engine's JSON type and PickleType stores arbitrary picklable Python objects in a BLOB. When the payload must come back as a typed entity, a small TypeDecorator implements process_bind_param/process_result_value over Text or LargeBinary - the documented extension point for exactly this (the same page shows the JSON-string recipe and the mutability caveat). Django's counterparts are JSONField with its encoder and a BinaryField plus an explicit codec. Pickle binds rows to a Python version and to class import paths, so prefer a JSON route for rows that outlive a deploy.
pitfalls: Plain JSON columns are not change-tracked: mutating the dict in place produces no UPDATE unless the column uses MutableDict/MutableList or flag_modified is called.
PickleType deserializes database content into live Python objects - loading a row executes whatever the payload names, so never load untrusted rows.
PickleType's default comparator unpickles both values to compare them, which is expensive and can raise for some types; set compare_values explicitly.
